In the middle slightly southwest part of the figure, near the 90° meridian, there is point F. Point F is close to the closed high-value area of the equal forest line marked as 4400 meters, and there is also a 4200-meter contour line around it, so the forest-line elevation at place F is about 4400 meters, and can be regarded as a high-value range of 4200–4400 meters. In the upper right part of the figure there is point E. The values of the equal forest lines near point E are obviously lower than those at point F, and it is in a low-value range of about 2800–3200 meters. Then reason: The question asks to compare the difference in forest-line elevation between place E and place F. Reading the values from the figure, place F is about 4400 meters, and place E is about 2800–3200 meters; the difference between the two is about 4400−3200 to 4400−2800, namely 1200–1600 meters.
